name: How deep should a kitchen peninsula be?

mainEntity.name: How deep should a kitchen peninsula be?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The right peninsula depth depends on whether it is for storage, prep, seating, or appliances. Standard base-cabinet depth may work for storage, while seating or opposing cabinets can require additional countertop depth and careful clearance planning.

Context: Homeowner discussions show that two-sided cabinet arrangements may need a deeper worktop and precise field measurements. A deeper peninsula can improve function but reduce walk space.

Key factors:
- Cabinet orientation and access from each side
- Seating overhang
- Appliance dimensions
- Remaining aisle width

Practical guidance: Decide which side needs drawers, doors, or seating before selecting depth. Have the countertop fabricated only after the installed cabinets are measured.

Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate cabinet configuration and countertop dimensions in the design phase.
acceptedAnswer.description: Depth depends on cabinet orientation, storage, seating, appliances, and remaining aisle space. Standard base-cabinet depth may be enough for one-sided storage, while seating or cabinets on both sides can require more depth. Confirm the full footprint before ordering the top.
